_meta.description: Starting points for common records-request topics, for people who know what they care about but not what to ask for.
_meta.two_layers: Every topic has generic_guidance and generic_want_template, which are true in general across Florida counties and never name a specific office. A topic MAY also have county_overrides — individually researched and sourced facts about one county's actual office and program names. The UI prefers a county_override when one exists for the selected county; otherwise it falls back to the generic template. This mirrors data/fl-counties.json: verified specifics or nothing, never a guess.
_meta.how_to_add_a_county_override: See CONTRIBUTING.md. Every override needs agency, want, source (one or more URLs), and verified (date). No override may be added without a real source to check against.
_meta.unpopulated_note: Most topic x county combinations have no override yet. That is expected, not a bug — coverage grows as people research and verify their own county, the same way poll_worker_url did.

topics.label: Environment & conservation
topics.generic_guidance: Land conservation and natural-resource spending is usually tracked by an environmental or natural resources department. Ask for spending and parcels or projects funded under any conservation land program, land-acquisition bond, or natural areas fund, over a specific date range.
topics.generic_want_template: Records showing spending under the county's environmental land conservation or natural areas program(s), and a list of parcels or projects funded, for [DATE RANGE].

county_overrides.agency: Palm Beach County Environmental Resources Management (ERM)
county_overrides.want: Records showing spending from the county's Natural Areas Fund and any related environmentally sensitive lands or land conservation bond funds, and a list of parcels acquired or under management as county natural areas, for [DATE RANGE].
county_overrides.notes: No single branded program name found. Funding flows through the Natural Areas Fund plus two historical bonds: the 1991 Environmentally Sensitive Lands Bond and the 1999 Land Acquisition for Conservation Purposes Referendum. Individual protected sites each have their own management plan.

topics.label: Government spending & contracts
topics.generic_guidance: Budgets are usually posted online, but who was actually paid for what often isn't. Ask for invoices, contracts, or payment records for a specific vendor, service, or department — the more specific the category, the easier it is to search for. Which office holds this varies more than most records: sometimes a Clerk of Court, sometimes a Finance or Comptroller's office.
topics.generic_want_template: Invoices, contracts, or payment records for [VENDOR, SERVICE, OR DEPARTMENT], covering [DATE RANGE].

topics.label: Government meeting records
topics.generic_guidance: Florida's Sunshine Law (Ch. 286, Fla. Stat.) requires most government meetings to be open and minuted. If minutes, a recording, or backup materials from a specific meeting aren't posted online, you can request them directly. Usually held by a Clerk of the Board or County Clerk.
topics.generic_want_template: Minutes, recordings, or backup materials from the [BOARD OR COMMISSION] meeting on [DATE].

topics.label: Roads & infrastructure
topics.generic_guidance: Repaving schedules, traffic studies, and infrastructure spending are usually handled by a Public Works or Engineering department. Ask about a specific road, project, or planning study rather than "all road records" — a named project is what turns this into a search someone can actually run.
topics.generic_want_template: Records showing the maintenance schedule, traffic study, or spending for [ROAD OR PROJECT NAME], covering [DATE RANGE].

topics.label: Public safety
topics.generic_guidance: Sheriff's offices hold records like incident reports, policies, budgets, and statistics. Florida's sheriffs are elected constitutional officers — one per county — so every county below has a verified office name and contact. Cities that run their own police department separately from the county sheriff aren't covered here; name the department yourself if that's who holds the record.
topics.generic_want_template: Records related to [a specific incident, policy, budget line, or statistic — name it], covering [DATE RANGE].
